title: US Denies Abbas Entry Visa for Second Straight Year; UN General Assembly Votes 152-3 to Let Him Address Body by Video
detail: The US State Department announced on Wednesday, September 16, 2026 that it would again deny Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas an entry visa to travel to New York for the UN General Assembly's annual leaders' week, extending broader visa sanctions against PLO and PA officials. The department said the measures respond to Palestinian officials' 'failure to reform,' their pursuit of statehood recognition and legal action against Israel at international tribunals 'to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian conflict,' and payments to individuals it labels attackers. On Thursday, September 17, the UN General Assembly voted 152 to 3, with 4 abstentions, to again allow Abbas to address the gathering by prerecorded video message -- the second consecutive year he has been barred from attending in person. The Palestinian Ministry of Foreign Affairs welcomed the resolution as 'breaking of the attempt to prevent Palestine's participation' and reaffirmed reliance on 'political, legal and diplomatic means.' Amnesty International condemned the US visa denial as a 'clear violation of the UN Headquarters Agreement,' saying Washington was misusing its host-country privileges to restrict UN participation in a manner not applied to Israeli officials.

media.caption: US President Donald Trump greets Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas at a summit in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, October 13, 2025 -- file photo illustrating US-PA relations

confidenceReason: The State Department's visa denial and the UN General Assembly's 152-3 vote are corroborated by multiple Tier 2 outlets across poles (Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, Haaretz) citing the same State Department statement and UNGA resolution.

title: Israel Opens Tender for 2,167 More E1 Settlement Units, Bringing Total to 3,401; Bidding Set for Two Days Before Knesset Election
detail: Israeli rights group Ir Amim said Wednesday, September 16-17, 2026 that Israel's government is opening bidding for an additional 2,167 housing units in the E1 settlement project east of Jerusalem, on top of a 1,234-unit tender announced in late August -- bringing the combined total to 3,401 housing units. The E1 tract of land runs from the outskirts of Jerusalem deep into the occupied West Bank; building it out would bisect the West Bank and sever East Jerusalem from the rest of the territory, fragmenting the land Palestinians hope will form the heart of a future state and connecting Jerusalem to the Ma'ale Adumim settlement bloc. The bidding is scheduled to open October 25, 2026, two days before Israel's Knesset election. Ir Amim said the timing reflected the government's resolve to 'create an increasingly irreversible reality on the ground ahead of the elections.' Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who greenlit E1 construction in August 2025, has said the project 'practically erases the two-state delusion.' Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas condemned the tender as a violation of international law; the Israeli Prime Minister's Office did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

media.caption: Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich presents the E1 settlement scheme map, August 14, 2025

confidenceReason: Tender figures and the October 25 bidding date are corroborated by Ir Amim (the monitoring group with direct access to Israeli planning records) and independently reported by a Tier 2 Israeli outlet and a Tier 3 international wire pickup; Smotrich's framing and Abbas's condemnation are each side's own characterization.
